fullPassage:
Keep Trying and Keep Hoping

People all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. Some have succeeded, some have failed, but remember that every little change helps.

Seaweed Hamburger Packages

Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025.

Your Leather Bags Are Going Un-Leather

What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.

questions.passage: People all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. Some have succeeded, some have failed, but remember that every little change ①<u>help</u>. Most food packaging is coated with plastic, ②<u>making</u> it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be ③<u>wrapped</u> in seaweed. A team of researchers ④<u>has</u> invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 모든 작은 변화가 도움이 된다(helps). help → helps. 주어 every little change(단수) → 동사 helps
det.analysis:
✅ ① help → helps: every + 단수명사 → 단수동사 필요. every little change helps
❌ ② making: 분사구문 (결과) 정상
❌ ③ wrapped: be wrapped in (수동태) 정상
❌ ④ has: a team(단수) → has invented 정상
det.tip: every + 단수명사 → 단수동사. every student has (O) / every student have (X)

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been ①<u>trying</u> to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, ②<u>when</u> a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been ③<u>testing</u>, and some have been proven ④<u>to make</u> alternative leathers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 많은 친환경 재료가 시험되었다(tested). testing → tested. have been + p.p. (수동태)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ testing → tested: have been tested (현재완료 수동태). ingredients가 시험을 '당하는' 것
❌ ① trying: have been trying (현재완료 진행형) 정상
❌ ② when: 시간의 관계부사 정상
❌ ④ to make: have been proven to V (to부정사) 정상
det.tip: have been + p.p. = 현재완료 수동태. have been + ~ing = 현재완료 진행형. 주어가 행위를 당하면 수동

questions.passage: The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from ①<u>sticking</u> to paper, while also breaking down more ②<u>easily</u> than plastic. The material can be made into thin films ③<u>that</u> can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands ④<u>plan</u> to choose greener packaging by 2025.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 주요 레스토랑 브랜드들이 더 친환경적인 포장을 선택할 계획을 하며(planning). plan → planning. with + 명사 + 현재분사(능동)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ plan → planning: 'with major restaurant brands planning' 부대상황 분사구문
❌ ① sticking: prevent A from ~ing (동명사) 정상
❌ ② easily: 비교급 more easily 정상
❌ ③ that: 주격 관계대명사, 선행사 films 수식 정상
det.tip: with + 명사 + V-ing(현재분사): 부대상황 구문. brands가 계획하는 것이므로 능동(planning)

questions.passage: Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom ①<u>grown</u> from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products ②<u>continues</u> to grow, more will be invented and ③<u>used</u>. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued ④<u>for</u> $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 시장은 7억 2,500만 달러로 평가되었다. for → at. be valued at = ~의 가치로 평가되다
det.analysis:
✅ ④ for → at: 'be valued at + 금액'이 올바른 전치사. be valued for는 '~때문에 가치있다'
❌ ① grown: 과거분사 (farming waste에서 재배된 버섯) 정상
❌ ② continues: demand(단수) → continues 정상
❌ ③ used: will be invented and used (수동태 병렬) 정상
det.tip: be valued at + 금액 = ~으로 평가되다. be valued for + 이유 = ~때문에 가치있다. 전치사 at 주의!

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new __________ material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새로운 코팅(coating) 소재는 거의 플라스틱처럼 작동한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① coating(코팅): 플라스틱 코팅을 대체하는 소재라는 문맥
❌ ② heating(가열): 포장 소재 문맥에 부적절
❌ ③ cleaning(세척): 포장 소재 문맥에 부적절
❌ ④ packaging(포장): 소재(material) 자체의 종류를 말하므로 coating이 정확
det.tip: coating material = 코팅 소재. 기존 플라스틱 코팅을 대체하는 새 소재

questions.passage: What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of ①<u>artificial</u> leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more ②<u>environmentally</u> friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' ③<u>disappointment</u>, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been ④<u>proven</u> to make alternative leathers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 많은 고객의 안도(relief)에 이르러. disappointment(실망)는 relief(안도)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ disappointment(실망) → relief(안도)가 원문. 친환경 대안이 발견되어 안심이라는 긍정 맥락
❌ ① artificial(인조의): 원문 그대로
❌ ② environmentally(환경적으로): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ proven(입증된): 원문 그대로
det.tip: relief(안도) ↔ disappointment(실망). 'To one's relief' = ~의 안도로

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"대부분의 식품 포장은 플라스틱으로 코팅되어 있어 재활용이 거의 불가능하다."

det.korean: 대부분의 식품 포장은 플라스틱으로 코팅되어 재활용이 거의 불가능하다. → 일치(T)
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문 'Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle'과 정확히 일치
❌ F: 원문 내용과 일치하므로 F는 오답
det.tip: nearly impossible = 거의 불가능한. coated with = ~으로 코팅된

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"석유 기반 가죽은 인조 가죽의 소수를 차지하며, 적은 에너지로 생산 가능하다."

det.korean: 석유 기반 가죽은 인조 가죽의 대다수(majority)를 차지하며, 많은(a lot of) 에너지를 필요로 한다. → 불일치(F)
det.analysis:
✅ F: '소수' → majority(대다수), '적은 에너지' → a lot of energy. 두 군데 모두 원문과 반대
❌ T: 원문과 두 곳이 다르므로 T는 오답
det.tip: majority(대다수) ≠ 소수, a lot of(많은) ≠ 적은. 패러프레이징 주의

questions.passage: The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"와인 산업의 포도 폐기물과 농업 폐기물에서 자란 버섯이 가죽 같은 시트로 만들어졌다."

det.korean: 포도 폐기물과 버섯이 가죽 같은 시트로 전환되었다. → 일치(T)
det.analysis:
✅ T: 'Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets'와 일치
❌ F: 원문 내용과 정확히 일치하므로 F는 오답
det.tip: turn into = ~로 전환하다. leather-like sheets = 가죽 같은 시트

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also __________. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: breaking down more easily than plastic

det.korean: 새 코팅 소재는 플라스틱처럼 작동하면서도 플라스틱보다 더 쉽게 분해된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② breaking down more easily than plastic: 플라스틱의 대안이므로 장점(쉬운 분해) 서술
❌ ① 생산 비용 증가: 장점을 나열하는 문맥에 부적절
❌ ③ 재활용을 더 어렵게: 환경 대안이므로 반대
❌ ④ 더 많은 에너지 필요: 장점 나열 맥락에 부적절
det.tip: while also ~: 추가 장점을 나열. helping prevent ~ while also breaking down ~ 두 장점 병렬

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: fewer companies will invest in leather research
the price of oil-based leather will decrease
more will be invented and used
consumers will lose interest in alternatives

det.korean: 소비자 수요가 계속 증가하면서, 더 많은 것이 발명되고 사용될 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ more will be invented and used: 수요 증가 → 더 많은 발명/사용이라는 논리적 인과
❌ ① 투자 감소: 수요 증가와 모순
❌ ② 석유 기반 가죽 가격 하락: 친환경 대안 논의와 무관
❌ ④ 관심 상실: 수요 증가와 정반대
det.tip: As ~ continues to grow, more will ~ : 증가하는 수요 → 더 많은 발명. 인과관계 파악이 핵심

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 해초 소재는 북호주 토착 해초에서 만들어졌다.
새 코팅 소재는 플라스틱보다 분해가 더 어렵다.
새 소재는 종이 표면에만 코팅할 수 있다.
패스트푸드 업계는 이 소식을 환영하고 있다.

det.korean: 패스트푸드 업계는 이 소식을 환영(welcoming)하고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 패스트푸드 업계가 소식을 환영: 원문 'The fast-food industry is welcoming the news' 일치
❌ ① 북호주 → South Australia(남호주). 방향 변조
❌ ② 분해가 더 어렵다 → more easily(더 쉽게). 반대로 변조
❌ ③ 종이에만 → various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. '만'은 오류
det.tip: 세부 정보 변조 주의: South(남) ↔ 북, more easily ↔ 더 어렵다, various ↔ ~만

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 석유 기반 가죽은 분해에 오랜 시간이 걸린다.
포도 폐기물이 가죽 같은 시트로 만들어졌다.

det.korean: 첫 성공은 1990년대(the 1990s)에 이루어졌다. 2000년대가 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 2000년대 → 1990s(1990년대). 시기 변조
❌ ① 원문 'a long time to break down' 일치
❌ ③ 원문 'Grape waste ~ turned into leather-like sheets' 일치
❌ ④ 원문 'valued at $725 million' 일치
det.tip: 시기 변조 주의: the 1990s(1990년대) ≠ 2000년대. 숫자/연도 세부 확인 필수

questions.passage: A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. ①The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper. ②The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces. ③Major restaurant brands are planning to choose greener packaging by 2025. ④Oil-based leathers require a lot of energy to produce and break down easily.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 원문의 내용과 다르게 서술된 문장은?

det.korean: 석유 기반 가죽은 분해에 오랜 시간이 걸린다. ④에서 break down easily(쉽게 분해된다)는 원문과 반대이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 'break down easily' → 원문은 'a long time to break down'(분해에 오랜 시간). easily 추가로 의미 반대
❌ ① 원문 내용 정확 반영
❌ ② 원문 내용 정확 반영
❌ ③ 원문 내용 정확 반영
det.tip: 원문: a long time to break down(분해에 오랜 시간) vs ④: break down easily(쉽게 분해). 정반대 서술

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"연구팀은 남호주 토착 해초에서 __________ 소재를 발명했다."

det.korean: 연구팀은 남호주 토착 해초에서 대안(alternative) 소재를 발명했다.
det.analysis: ✅ alternative: 원문 'an alternative material from seaweed'에서 찾을 수 있음
det.tip: alternative = 대안의, 대체의. an alternative material = 대안 소재

questions.passage: As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was __________ (value) at $725 million.
questions.stem: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 2022년에 시장은 7억 2,500만 달러로 평가되었다(was valued).
det.analysis: ✅ valued: was + __________ → 수동태. value → valued (과거분사)
det.tip: be valued at = ~으로 평가되다. was valued = 수동태 과거

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, __________.
questions.stem:

[tested / many / been / since / other / then / ingredients / eco-friendly / have]
questions.wa: since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested
accept: since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested
since then many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested
Since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested
Since then many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested

det.korean: 그 이후로 많은 다른 친환경 재료가 시험되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested: 원문 문장 순서 그대로
det.tip: since then = 그 이후로. have been tested = 현재완료 수동태 (시험되어 왔다)

The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025.

questions.passage: What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will be invented and used.
